lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: inference from a sample to a population
lessonRef.title: Reteach and varied practice: inference from a sample to a population

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: These two examples show the same idea in two different formats.

items.prompt: n = 400, sample proportion 55%. Margin and interval?
3 of 500 simulations were as extreme. Conclusion?

steps: Below 5%, so the result is significant.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Work these with your teaching parent. Say the reason for each step out loud before you write it.

items.prompt: A quantity is approximately normal with mean 102 and standard deviation 3. Approximately what percentage of values lie between 96 and 108?
A researcher runs a randomised controlled experiment with participants randomly assigned to treatments. What kind of conclusion does this design support?
choices: It supports both generalisation and causation, provided the sample is large.
It supports a causal conclusion about the treatment, within the population studied.
It supports generalising from the sample to the population, but not a causal claim.
It supports neither generalisation nor causation, because self-selection can bias both.

items.prompt: A random sample of 100 people gives a sample proportion of 64%. Using the conservative margin of error 1/√n, give the approximate margin of error and the resulting interval.
In 1000 simulations under the assumption of no difference, 24 produced a result at least as extreme as the one observed. What should be concluded?
choices: The observed result is not statistically significant: it occurred in 2.4% of simulations, which is not unusual.
The simulation proves that the observed difference is real.
The simulation proves that there is no difference.
The observed result is statistically significant: it occurred in only 2.4% of simulations, below the usual 5% threshold.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A quantity is approximately normal with mean 63 and standard deviation 8. Approximately what percentage of values lie between 55 and 71?
A researcher runs an observational study of volunteers who chose their own group. What kind of conclusion does this design support?
choices: It supports generalising from the sample to the population, but not a causal claim.
It supports both generalisation and causation, provided the sample is large.
It supports neither generalisation nor causation, because self-selection can bias both.
It supports a causal conclusion about the treatment, within the population studied.

items.prompt: A random sample of 2500 people gives a sample proportion of 30%. Using the conservative margin of error 1/√n, give the approximate margin of error and the resulting interval.
In 1000 simulations under the assumption of no difference, 8 produced a result at least as extreme as the one observed. What should be concluded?
choices: The observed result is statistically significant: it occurred in only 0.8% of simulations, below the usual 5% threshold.
The observed result is not statistically significant: it occurred in 0.8% of simulations, which is not unusual.
The simulation proves that there is no difference.
The simulation proves that the observed difference is real.

items.prompt: A quantity is approximately normal with mean 108 and standard deviation 5. Approximately what percentage of values lie between 93 and 123?
